title: Vegetarian Dish Sales Share per Restaurant
description_markdown: Product team request: For each restaurant, calculate total menu items as `total_items`, and count of vegetarian options as `veg_items`. starter_query:
-- Menu vegetarian breakdown
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT r.name, r.cuisine, COUNT(m.item_id) AS total_items, SUM(CASE WHEN m.is_vegetarian = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS veg_items FROM restaurants r JOIN menu_items m ON r.restaurant_id = m.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name, r.cuisine HAVING COUNT(m.item_id) >= 2 ORDER BY veg_items DESC, r.restaurant_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses MySQL SUM(CASE ...) conditional aggregation to analyze menu composition.
common_mistakes: Using PostgreSQL FILTER (WHERE ...) clause which is not supported in MySQL.
dialect_notes: MySQL uses SUM(CASE WHEN condition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) for conditional counts.
hints: Use `SUM(CASE WHEN m.is_vegetarian = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS veg_items`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT r.name, r.cuisine, COUNT(m.item_id) AS total_items, SUM(CASE WHEN m.is_vegetarian = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS veg_items FROM restaurants r JOIN menu_items m ON r.restaurant_id = m.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name, r.cuisine HAVING COUNT(m.item_id) >= 2 ORDER BY veg_items DESC, r.restaurant_id ASC;

title: Track Successive Order Timestamps per Restaurant
description_markdown: For each delivery order, fetch the timestamp of the next consecutive order placed at the same restaurant as `next_order_time` using `LEAD()`. Return `order_id`, `restaurant_id`, `order_timestamp`, and `next_order_time`. Order by `restaurant_id` ASC, `order_timestamp` ASC, `order_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT order_id, restaurant_id, order_timestamp, LEAD(order_timestamp, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY order_timestamp ASC, order_id ASC) AS next_order_time FROM delivery_orders ORDER BY restaurant_id ASC, order_timestamp ASC, order_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses LEAD(order_timestamp, 1) partitioned by restaurant_id.
hints: Use `LEAD(order_timestamp, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY order_timestamp ASC, order_id ASC)`.
Order by `restaurant_id` ASC, `order_timestamp` ASC, `order_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT order_id, restaurant_id, order_timestamp, LEAD(order_timestamp, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY restaurant_id ORDER BY order_timestamp ASC, order_id ASC) AS next_order_time FROM delivery_orders ORDER BY restaurant_id ASC, order_timestamp ASC, order_id ASC;

title: Audit Menu Offerings with Zero Customer Orders
description_markdown: Find all menu items that have never been included in any customer order. Return `item_id`, `item_name`, and `price`. Order by `item_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT m.item_id, m.item_name, m.price FROM menu_items m LEFT JOIN delivery_order_items doi ON m.item_id = doi.item_id WHERE doi.order_item_id IS NULL ORDER BY m.item_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Anti-join using LEFT JOIN and filtering WHERE doi.order_item_id IS NULL.
hints: LEFT JOIN `delivery_order_items doi` on `m.item_id = doi.item_id`.
Filter with `WHERE doi.order_item_id IS NULL`.
Query: SELECT m.item_id, m.item_name, m.price FROM menu_items m LEFT JOIN delivery_order_items doi ON m.item_id = doi.item_id WHERE doi.order_item_id IS NULL ORDER BY m.item_id ASC;

title: Calculate Average Order Value per Restaurant
description_markdown: For each restaurant with delivered orders, calculate the average order total amount rounded to 2 decimals as `avg_order_value`. Return `name` and `avg_order_value`. Order by `avg_order_value` DESC, `name` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT r.name, ROUND(AVG(o.total_amount), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM restaurants r JOIN delivery_orders o ON r.restaurant_id = o.restaurant_id WHERE o.delivery_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC, r.name ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins restaurants and delivery_orders, filters on delivered, and computes ROUND(AVG(total_amount), 2).
hints: Filter with `WHERE o.delivery_status = 'delivered'`.
Compute `ROUND(AVG(o.total_amount), 2) AS avg_order_value`.

Query: SELECT r.name, ROUND(AVG(o.total_amount), 2) AS avg_order_value FROM restaurants r JOIN delivery_orders o ON r.restaurant_id = o.restaurant_id WHERE o.delivery_status = 'delivered' GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC, r.name ASC;

title: Identify Top Grossing Dish by Cumulative Sales Revenue
description_markdown: Calculate total revenue generated per menu item (`quantity * item_price`) as `total_item_revenue`. Return `item_name` and `total_item_revenue`. Order by `total_item_revenue` DESC, `item_name` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT m.item_name, SUM(doi.quantity * doi.item_price) AS total_item_revenue FROM menu_items m JOIN delivery_order_items doi ON m.item_id = doi.item_id GROUP BY m.item_id, m.item_name ORDER BY total_item_revenue DESC, m.item_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins menu_items and delivery_order_items and sums product of quantity and price.
hints: Calculate revenue with `SUM(doi.quantity * doi.item_price)`.
Group by `m.item_id, m.item_name`.

Query: SELECT m.item_name, SUM(doi.quantity * doi.item_price) AS total_item_revenue FROM menu_items m JOIN delivery_order_items doi ON m.item_id = doi.item_id GROUP BY m.item_id, m.item_name ORDER BY total_item_revenue DESC, m.item_name ASC;

title: Compile Food Delivery Marketplace Executive KPI Scorecard
description_markdown: Produce single-row marketplace operations summary metrics: `total_restaurants`, `active_drivers`, `delivered_orders`, and `total_gmv` (sum of delivered order amounts).
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM restaurants) AS total_restaurants, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM delivery_drivers WHERE is_active = TRUE) AS active_drivers, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM delivery_orders WHERE delivery_status = 'delivered') AS delivered_orders, (SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM delivery_orders WHERE delivery_status = 'delivered') AS total_gmv;
solution_explanation: Uses scalar subqueries to build an executive marketplace scorecard.
hints: Use scalar subqueries for each metric.
Sum total_amount for delivered orders.

Query: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM restaurants) AS total_restaurants, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM delivery_drivers WHERE is_active = TRUE) AS active_drivers, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM delivery_orders WHERE delivery_status = 'delivered') AS delivered_orders, (SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM delivery_orders WHERE delivery_status = 'delivered') AS total_gmv;
